findings.title: Evening and affected crying stage a report
findings.claim: The evening frame and the image of affected crying meet to make the brothers' arrival readable as a scene where emotional appearance helps carry the report.
findings.mechanism: The focus word for evening supplies the temporal frame and the focus verb supplies ongoing crying; the supplied cross-ayah relation adds a wider image of an internally embellished rationale joined to a material trace, allowing time and affect to function together as a persuasive setting.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the time word matters beside the crying: the arrival is presented through an emotional display before its factual basis becomes inspectable.
findings.containment: The literal evening arrival and the brothers' crying remain intact. The relation describes a possible staging function for the display and does not by itself prove deliberate feigning.

epistemic.reason: The focus time branch is registered with qualified boundaries and the crying image is a nominated branch; the reader-walk support and target connection supply the relation, but the target row lacks target morphology and the ambiguous alternative mapping is excluded.
